completenessChecks: Bold opening quotation with its attribution, five narration paragraphs, seven prompts with their answers, the closing paragraph and the sidebar caption are all present in the Hebrew order.

The one block-count difference is deliberate: the Hebrew prints the sixth prompt broken across two bold paragraphs (a publisher line break mid-sentence); the English joins it into one bold prompt. Seven distinct prompts in both languages.
The publicist's 'Last question' and the narration that follows stay inside the fifth answer paragraph, as in the Hebrew.
Names, ages, dates and film credits checked against the Hebrew; the historical wording was not corrected (see sourceProblems).
No hyperlinks in the Hebrew body; none added. No em dashes.
voiceChecks: Long-then-short rhythm kept: 'Fashionably late, of course.' 'Not so much as one blown kiss was recorded.' 'Oh well.' all stand as their own short sentences.
Mock-honorifics carried at the same weight: 'Her Grace', 'the lady', 'La Lopez' (for the Hebrew definite article on her name), 'the nation's sweetheart'.

Formal-next-to-street collision kept where the Hebrew has it: 'as befits a girl who goes through journalists like roasted pistachios'; 'the day is short and the work is plentiful, so come on, let's talk' (the Pirkei Avot phrase next to yalla).
Narrator stays the foil: trembling heart, battered kitten, glared at; nothing was added to make him look sharper.
The Don Corleone callback and the 'maybe that schizophrenia is the secret of her charm' judgment stay in the final paragraph, framed as impression, with the concession intact.
Serious material (the battered-woman plot, Katrina) rendered straight.
Quotations given spoken English ('lost her mind', 'didn't rattle me', 'nobody gets to call me at two in the morning anymore') without adding content or fixing logic.

decisions: Headline: the Hebrew 'ג'יי לא' puns J.Lo against 'J. no'; 'J. No' does the same job in English and is kept.
Subtitle rebuilt as three 'Could we...' questions ending in 'and call it a day?', then 'Nimrod Dvir went to meet Her Grace, and the two fell out, badly' for 'הסתכסך קשות'.
'מידותיה הנאות' (virtues / measurements) rendered 'fine proportions', which keeps a faint double sense.
'אוכלת עיתונאים כמו פיסטוקים קלויים' rendered 'goes through journalists like roasted pistachios' (literal comparison kept, verb made idiomatic).
'חמולת הפמליה שלה' rendered 'the clan she calls an entourage'.
'עלתה לנו בפרנסה' rendered 'just cost us a day's pay' rather than the stiff 'cost us our livelihood'.
'דרוכה לפתע כסוהרת גרמנייה' rendered 'suddenly bristling like a German prison matron'.
'רוברט רדפורד בפוזת קאובוי' rendered 'Robert Redford, in cowboy mode'; 'נוסעת להתנחל אצל' rendered 'goes to park herself at the home of'.

Established titles: An Unfinished Life, Enough (for 'עד כאן'), Chocolat, The Cider House Rules. Established spellings: Lasse Hallström, Damian Lewis, Becca Gardner, Marc Anthony, Imelda Marcos, Ora Namir, Sarit Hadad.
The publisher's mid-sentence split of the sixth prompt was joined into one bold prompt; the Hebrew file keeps the split.
Sidebar caption kept under its provenance comment, as in the reference files; 'רויטרס' rendered 'Reuters'.

The definite article joke in 'הלופז' is approximated by 'La Lopez'.
